solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Use Bob’s lad devised for instrument (6,4)

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into a new arrangement, as a plan is devised

explanation.surface: A boy called Bob has come up with a use for a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Bob’s is ignored: only the letters USE BOBS LAD count.
explanation.definitionFit: The double bass is the largest bowed string instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: Queen was lazy? (4)

blocks.note: a queen of classical legend, ruler of Carthage
someone lazy did nothing, and O is the crossword’s nought

explanation.surface: A question about whether some queen was idle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second definition as a pun: someone lazy 'did O', that is did nothing, with O standing for zero. Split differently it is Dido.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the queen of Carthage who loved Aeneas in Virgil’s Aeneid.

clue.text: Ill-natured opening to game in part of summer without leader (4)

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
G goes inside what follows
the leading letter is dropped

blocks.note: JULY, a summer month, loses its first letter J

explanation.surface: Some bad-tempered start to a game played during the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of summer' is a month, July in the northern calendar; beheaded it is ULY, and G slips in after the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean hostile or bad-tempered, as in an ugly mood.

clue.text: Change in Ulster gaining distinction (6)

indicators.note: the letters of Ulster are changed around

explanation.surface: A political change in Northern Ireland wins the province some honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland, much of it now Northern Ireland; here it is just six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is glory or distinction, as in adding lustre to a reputation.

clue.text: A fair bit getting attention? (6,9)

blocks.note: reads as 'quite a lot', but fair can mean light-haired and bit is old slang for a young woman
reads as something noticed, but means a woman who turns heads wherever she goes

explanation.surface: A reasonable amount of something that earns notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fair bit' reads as 'quite a lot', but fair means light-haired and bit is old slang for a young woman; a blonde bombshell is exactly one who draws attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A blonde bombshell is a strikingly attractive fair-haired woman.

clue.text: Still enthralled by contest at ice-skating (6)

indicators.note: the answer is held captive inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone remains captivated by an ice-skating competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as 'yet', an adverb, but it is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something static stays in one place, which is what still means as an adjective.

clue.text: Bishops, perhaps, beginning to discourage reform (4)

indicators.note: bishops are an example of chessmen, so an example stands for the class
the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: bishops are chess pieces, or men

explanation.surface: Churchmen setting out to put people off reform.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts bishops in the church; the answer wants them on a chessboard, where the pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean putting right what was wrong, as in mending one’s ways; reform is used of habits, mend of habits and objects alike.

clue.text: Review so often dry? No further discussion needed (3,2,5)

indicators.note: the letters are looked over and redone

explanation.surface: A critic complaining that a show is often tedious, and that is all there is to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review' looks like a theatre critic’s piece, but it tells you to re-view, that is rework, the letters of 'so often dry'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'End of story' is said to close a subject: nothing more to discuss.

clue.text: Consider composer lacking special value (10)

indicators.note: the composer’s name goes without the letter named

blocks.note: DELIBES, the French composer of Coppélia, loses S for special

explanation.surface: Weighing up a composer who has no particular worth.
explanation.walkthrough: Léo Delibes wrote the ballets Coppélia and Sylvia; S is the standard abbreviation for special.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: weighing a question at length before deciding, as a jury does.

clue.text: Unusual lines aloud harbouring fantasies? (10)

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An actor speaking strange lines out loud while caught up in daydreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aloud' looks like a sound signal, but it is simply five of the ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone delusional holds false beliefs, fantasies they cling to.

clue.text: Celebration held by the Italian star (4)

indicators.note: what is held by something sits within its grasp, so the celebration goes inside the Italian article

explanation.surface: A party thrown by an Italian film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Italian' means the Italian word for the, IL; a do is informal British for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop or film star worshipped by fans is their idol; the religious sense of an image worshipped lies underneath.

clue.text: Make fine distinctions composing parish list (5,5)

indicators.note: the letters are put together into a new form

explanation.surface: A vicar fussing over the exact wording of a parish register.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder sits straight after the indicator and uses every letter of both words.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: dividing something as thin as a hair pictures distinctions too fine to matter.

clue.text: Stuffy ring about serving men? That’s rudimentary (10)

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, the enlisted soldiers
to ring is to dial, and 'about' sets the serving men beside it

explanation.surface: A starchy person calling round about the servants and being told that is basic stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Other ranks, the soldiers who are not officers, is a standard crossword abbreviation. 'About' is loose here: it sets the ring beside the serving men rather than around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Primordial means existing from the beginning, in its earliest, most rudimentary form.

clue.text: First couple of deliveries carried by transport as part of deal? (5-2)

indicators.note: keep the first two letters
DE is carried inside TRAIN, as passengers are

blocks.note: a train is a means of transport

explanation.surface: The first two parcels loaded onto a lorry as part of a business arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a trade-in is only one possible part of a deal: the old car handed over towards the new one.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an item given in part payment when buying something new.

clue.text: Mad sort planned despotic rule (7)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged to a new plan

explanation.surface: A lunatic has plotted a tyranny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like the indicator; it is fodder, and 'planned' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsardom is rule by a tsar, the byword for autocracy.

clue.text: Short work made by star absorbing English lines (7)

indicators.note: the star takes E and LL inside it

blocks.note: a nova is a star that flares up

explanation.surface: A famous actor soaking up English verse to produce a brief piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity, but here it is the astronomical nova.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a piece of fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novel, so a short work.

clue.text: Study country with extremists in senate (6)

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of senate

explanation.surface: Looking into a nation whose senate is full of radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' reads as political radicals, but it means the extreme letters, S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean examining a text closely, though peruse is often misused for skimming.

clue.text: Chat regarding fellow in taxi (6)

indicators.note: the fellow is sitting in the taxi, so those letters go inside the word for it

explanation.surface: Talking about a man sitting in a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: The taxi setting fits the answer neatly: a confab is the kind of chat a cabbie has with a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab, short for confabulation, is an informal chat.

clue.text: I harmonise meter having changed electrical apparatus (9,6)

indicators.note: the letters have been changed around

explanation.surface: A poet who has tinkered with the metre of a verse, or an electrician with a meter.
explanation.walkthrough: An immersion heater is the electric element in a British hot-water tank, often just called 'the immersion'.
explanation.definitionFit: An immersion heater is an electrical element that sits in water to heat it.

clue.text: Price was paid for this tearaway? (6)

blocks.note: Vincent Price, the actor, earned his living in one film genre
a tearaway is a wild, unruly youngster

explanation.surface: Someone paid a high price for an unruly youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: Price is capitalised because it is the actor Vincent Price, star of 1950s and 1960s horror films; a tearaway is a reckless young person.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror was Vincent Price’s paid trade, and a horror is also a badly behaved child.

clue.text: A recipe taken up with relish for stew (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: R = recipe, the Latin 'take' heading prescriptions
gout, from French goût, is taste or relish

explanation.surface: A cook following a recipe with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: The R for recipe is the Rx sign on prescriptions; GOUT here is not the joint disease but the old borrowing of French goût, taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned French stew.

clue.text: Possibly, vintage Cambridge college close to street (6)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An old Cambridge college standing near a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vintage' reads as 'old' describing the college, but it is the definition: a claret may be a vintage wine, hence 'possibly'. Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret, red Bordeaux, is a wine that may well be a vintage.

clue.text: 150 in ICU falling short in hospital (6)

indicators.note: ICU is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: ICU with its final U dropped

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty patients in intensive care, with the hospital short of beds.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is part of the wordplay, the second joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a place for medical treatment, often a small or specialist hospital.

clue.text: Sadly a sign to withdraw wine (7)

indicators.note: the whole string draws back, read right to left

blocks.note: the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Unhappily, it is a signal to give up drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sign' is not a signal but one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, Aries, whose symbol is the ram; the whole string is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily, named after the port it is shipped from.

clue.text: Woman from Dublin perhaps rejecting hotel (4)

indicators.note: to reject something is to throw it out, so the hotel’s letter is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: H = hotel in the NATO alphabet; removed

explanation.surface: A Dublin woman turning down a hotel room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' admits Dublin is only one example of somewhere Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Iris is a woman’s first name, borne for instance by the novelist Iris Murdoch.

clue.text: Opposed to prank clubs banned (4)

indicators.note: C for clubs is banned from the word

blocks.note: C = clubs, the card suit; removed

explanation.surface: Someone against a joke that got certain clubs shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests societies or nightclubs, but it is the card suit, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti is a preposition in its own right, as in 'anti the war', so it swaps straight for 'opposed to'.

clue.text: Report of how things turn out in charitable event (4)

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the answer sounds like the word

blocks.note: fate is how things turn out

explanation.surface: A news report on how some charity event went.
explanation.walkthrough: A fete is a British outdoor fundraiser with stalls and games, usually for a church or school.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor event held to raise money for a cause.

clue.text: Control nag once very wild with no end of energy (10)

indicators.note: the letters run wild into a new order
the end letter of energy, Y, is taken out of VERY

blocks.note: used as it stands, before a letter is removed
last letter of energy, taken out of VERY to leave VER

explanation.surface: Reining in an old horse that used to be wild and has now run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y removed is the end of 'energy', not of 'very'; they just happen to share it.
explanation.definitionFit: Governance is the exercise of authority over an organisation or country, so control in the managerial sense.

clue.text: Rugby club offering goods at reduced price (4)

definitions.note: a sale is the event, not the goods themselves

blocks.note: an English rugby union club, named after its town near Manchester
the shop event where prices are cut

explanation.surface: A rugby club selling off merchandise cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: Sale is a town near Manchester whose rugby union team is Sale Sharks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale is an event where goods are sold at reduced prices.

clue.text: A hanging for a caveman? (10)

blocks.note: reads as an execution or a tapestry, but means anything that hangs down
someone living in a cave would have rock formations dangling from the ceiling as décor

explanation.surface: A prehistoric man sentenced to the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests execution or a tapestry; the caveman’s decoration is the rock formation hanging from his cave’s ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalactite is a column of mineral deposit hanging from a cave roof.
